source_identity: LinkML CLI documentation — linkml validate, linkml-lint (Schema Linter), gen-erdiagram, and Subsets docs pages
source_family: linkml-official-docs (same family as source-linkml-metamodel.json; both drawn from linkml.io/linkml)
precise_evidence_location: https://linkml.io/linkml/cli/validate.html ('linkml validate' command reference, --exit-on-first-failure option); https://linkml.io/linkml/schemas/linter.html (Schema Linter rule list and exit-code section); https://linkml.io/linkml/generators/erdiagram.html (gen-erdiagram --format option and PNG/PDF limitation note); https://linkml.io/linkml/schemas/subsets.html (in_subset slot description).
method: Direct retrieval of the named LinkML documentation pages, reading CLI reference tables and narrative limitation statements verbatim.
limitations: The `linkml validate` CLI reference page documents an --exit-on-first-failure flag but does not itself state numeric exit codes for success vs. failure in the text captured; the exit-code behavior recorded here for that specific command is therefore an operational gap flagged in contrary_evidence_search, distinct from the Schema Linter page, which does document explicit exit codes (0/1/2). Readers should not conflate the two: `linkml validate` (data/schema instance validation) and the Schema Linter (`linkml-lint`, schema-authoring style checks) are two different LinkML CLI tools with two different documented behaviors. The erdiagram page's PNG/PDF statement is dated by its own wording ('There is currently no way...') without a page timestamp, so it is uncertain whether this remains true at the exact v1.11.1 release; no contrary evidence of a newer PNG/SVG capability was found in the same search pass (see contrary_evidence_search).

raw_evidence.quote: Validate data against a LinkML schema, or validate a schema itself against the metamodel.

When -s/--schema is omitted, positional arguments are treated as schema files and validated against the LinkML metamodel — verifying required fields, correct types, valid URIs, and NCName constraints.
--exit-on-first-failure: Exit after the first validation failure is found. If not specified all validation failures are reported.
canonical_prefixes, no_empty_title, no_invalid_slot_usage, no_xsd_int_type, permissible_values_format, recommended, standard_naming, tree_root_class
Exit 0: No violations detected; Exit 2: Any level: error violations present; Exit 1 (default): Only level: warning violations found
By default, the output includes markdown fence blocks
There is currently no way to directly generate PNGs/PDFs/etc from the mermaid code. You can use the mermaid live editor to generate these.
The in_subset slot can be used tag your class (or slot) to belong to a pre-defined subset.

validator_exit_code.citation: cli/validate.html --exit-on-first-failure option; schemas/linter.html documented Exit 0/1/2 codes
validator_exit_code.rationale: Two separate LinkML tools exist. `linkml-lint` (the Schema Linter) has clearly documented, graduated exit codes (0 clean, 1 warnings only, 2 any errors) and so can sit behind a deterministic CI gate directly, comparable to `structurizr validate`. `linkml validate` (data/schema-instance validation against the metamodel) is documented to report failures and offers an --exit-on-first-failure flag, but the fetched page text does not state its numeric exit-code contract on failure, so its suitability as a CI gate on malformed/inconsistent SCHEMAS specifically (as opposed to data) is not fully confirmed from this page alone — classified as workaround-dependent (use linkml-lint for schema gating, where the exit-code contract is explicit) rather than a single clean 'validator with documented non-zero exit' answer across both tools.

svg_export_from_container.citation: generators/erdiagram.html limitations note: 'There is currently no way to directly generate PNGs/PDFs/etc from the mermaid code.'
svg_export_from_container.rationale: gen-erdiagram's only documented outputs are markdown/mermaid text, not SVG. The page explicitly states there is no way to generate PNG/PDF (and by extension no documented SVG path) from the generated mermaid text using LinkML's own tooling; the documented workaround is an external tool (the mermaid live editor), which is outside LinkML's own toolchain and not shown to be scriptable inside a Docker container with no local install.

png_export_from_container.rationale: Same finding as SVG: the documentation states directly and explicitly that PNG generation from LinkML's own ER-diagram output is not currently possible without an external, non-containerized tool (mermaid live editor).

named_subset_views_for_diagram_splitting.rationale: The documented `subsets`/`in_subset` mechanism is described only as a tagging/annotation feature ('can be used to tag your class ... to belong to a pre-defined subset'). No text on this page, nor cross-referenced from the erdiagram generator page, describes subsets being consumed to filter or split a generated diagram into a named sub-view the way Structurizr views do. Diagram generation (gen-erdiagram) and the subsets annotation appear to be two independent, undocumented-as-connected features in the pages examined.

search_terms: linkml validate exit code schema malformed
where_searched: general web search (WebSearch tool), no domain restriction
contrary_evidence_search.result: No explicit numeric exit-code statement was found on the linkml-validate (data/schema instance validator) page itself, unlike the Schema Linter page which states exit codes explicitly — recorded as a genuine documentation gap rather than inferred. No documentation was found describing gen-erdiagram routing through mermaid-cli, graphviz, or any other renderer for SVG/PNG output; the page's own text states this is not currently possible. No documentation was found connecting `subsets`/`in_subset` to diagram generation or to any view-splitting feature — the absence is recorded as a definite negative finding for named subset views over a rendered diagram.
